title: Baked Bites: how Frisco students turned a passion for baking into a force for community change | The Optimist Daily
text:
A new solution in your inbox every day.

BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM

At a Baked Bites pop-up in Frisco, Texas, the transaction looks simple: you place a pre-order, you pick up a homemade cookie. Buried inside that small exchange, though, is something more considered. Every dollar goes to charity, and the students packaging those orders have made that the only condition.

Since launching, Baked Bites has raised more than $8,000 for charitable causes, primarily through its partnership with Frisco Fastpacs, a nonprofit that delivers weekend meal bags to more than 1,200 food-insecure children across Frisco ISD every Friday of the school year. For many of those kids, the bags are the primary source of food when school is not in session.

Baked Bites is a student-led nonprofit. The founders, Dyuthi Bushipaga, Aditi Puri, Twinkle Jadhav, and Harika Yerramchetty, all grew up in Frisco, in the same school district that Frisco Fastpacs serves. They chose to use what they had- a skill for baking and a willingness to show up- to do something about what they saw.

The model’s simplicity is part of its strategy: homemade baked goods, sold through pre-orders and at community pop-ups, with all proceeds going directly to their charity partner. There is no corporate backing or overhead designed to extract from the mission. Just students, cookies, and a community that keeps buying them.

The founders are clear about what that number means to them: not a fundraising milestone, but hundreds of people who chose to spend a few dollars on a cookie and, in doing so, chose to believe their neighbor’s hunger was worth solving.

There is something instructive about the math of small acts. A single weekend bag from Frisco Fastpacs costs the organization very little to fill. Enough of those small purchases, from enough people who showed up to a pop-up or placed a pre-order, and you have fed a lot of children over a lot of Saturdays.

This summer was Baked Bites’ biggest season yet. Seven to eight bake sales, pop-ups, and community collaborations, each one a chance to bring new people into the loop and expand what the organization can fund.

Their model is highly replicable, and they have expanded their reach with 15 Baked Bites ambassadors from different schools in Texas and California.

Looking further ahead, the group hopes to partner with more local schools to connect students with resources and encouragement they might not otherwise encounter. And it’s going further than access to food.

They have already had 18+ partnerships, ranging from giving kids opportunities to learn coding to initiatives that help people step away from screens. The team even launched a second Instagram account to share some positive ‘bites of wisdom’.

It is a modest extension of the same instinct that started with selling their homemade sweets: help the people around you with what you have, and keep going. What a sweet solution.

Pre-order details are available through their Instagram, @bbaked_bites, or on their website for anyone in the Frisco area.
